description: Lokalna single-user aplikacja webowa do tworzenia i przechodzenia interaktywnych kursów. Architektura: Next.js (App Router) + TS + Tailwind + shadcn/ui. Persystencja plikowa: kursy w /courses/<slug>/ jako JSON, postęp w ~/.ai-lecturer/progress.json. Lekcje to statyczne artefakty (sekcje + widgety) generowane offline przez ralph loop przy użyciu skili init_course / generate_lesson — webapp tylko renderuje, edytuje, i zbiera spec do generacji. Widgety MVP: theory (markdown + KaTeX), quiz ABCD, code exercise z Pyodide i ukrytymi testami, demo Gauss filter, sandbox. Wizualnie wysoka wierność do specyfikacji w claude/design/ (tokens.css → CSS vars konsumowane przez Tailwind). LessonChat (AI tutor) i live agent log są poza MVP.

Course card status badge derived as: 0 lessons started → 'New'; any started but not all finished → 'In progress · X/Y' (X=finished count, Y=total lessons); all finished → 'Completed'
Course card progress bar fill = finishedCount / totalLessons
Continue learning hero on dashboard reads lastVisitedAt across all courses, picks the one with the latest timestamp, shows its lastVisitedLessonSlug

When the user clicks Mark complete in lesson view (US-018) and returns to dashboard via prev navigation or 'All courses' link, dashboard reflects new status without manual refresh (refetch on focus is enough)
TOC dots in lesson view live-update when current lesson is marked complete (no full reload required)
Verify in browser using playwright-skill: complete one lesson, return to dashboard, confirm card badge changes to 'In progress · 1/N' and hero shows that course
Typecheck passes

stories.title: Theme toggle (light/dark) in dashboard header + lesson toolbar
stories.description: As a learner, I want a sun/moon button in both the dashboard header and the lesson toolbar to switch between light and dark mode, with my choice remembered.
acceptanceCriteria: <ThemeToggle /> component renders a 28px icon button: shows sun icon when current data-theme='dark' (clicking → switches to light), moon icon when current data-theme='light' (clicking → switches to dark)
Click toggles <html data-theme> attribute and persists choice to localStorage['theme']
On app boot: an inline blocking script in <head> reads localStorage['theme'] and applies before React hydrates (prevents FOUC); fallback: prefers-color-scheme when localStorage['theme'] unset
Mounted in dashboard header (between settings and avatar) AND in lesson toolbar (between section progress pill and shortcuts button '?')
120ms transition on icon swap (opacity + 180° rotate)
Respects prefers-color-scheme on first load only; subsequent loads honor user's last manual choice

Verify in browser using playwright-skill: load dashboard in light mode, click toggle, confirm CSS vars switch (background changes, all sample swatches recolor); reload page, confirm dark mode persisted; same flow inside a lesson view
Typecheck passes

stories.title: Keyboard shortcuts + shortcuts modal
stories.description: As a learner, I want comprehensive keyboard navigation in the lesson view and a shortcuts modal showing all bindings, so I can move through lessons without a mouse.
acceptanceCriteria: Global hook src/lib/hooks/useKeyboardShortcuts.ts registers handlers; ignores keys when active element is input/textarea/contentEditable/CodeMirror

Lesson view shortcuts: j or ↓ → next section (smooth scroll to next #section-…), k or ↑ → previous section, ⌘B → toggle TOC, ⌘. → toggle tutor (no-op visible state in MVP), Space → mark current section complete (if section supports it), n → next lesson when current marked complete, p → previous lesson, f → focus mode (collapses both panels)
Global: '?' opens shortcuts modal, Esc closes any open modal

Shortcuts modal: list grouped by category (Global / Lesson / Code editor / Chat composer); each row shows the key combo (in --font-mono in a small pill) + action description; styled per design tokens with --bg-elevated, --radius-xl, max-width 520px, 1px --border; backdrop blur-sm + 50% black overlay; click backdrop or Esc closes
@media (prefers-reduced-motion: reduce) disables smooth scrolling triggered by j/k
Verify in browser using playwright-skill: press '?', screenshot modal in light + dark; press Esc, confirm closed; press 'j' in a lesson, confirm scrollY increases
Typecheck passes

stories.title: Inline edit for Theory widget — markdown editor + preview
stories.description: As a course author, I want to edit theory markdown directly in the lesson view with a live preview so I can polish content without leaving the app.
acceptanceCriteria: Theory widget header gets an 'Edit' icon button (pencil) in addition to existing controls
Click 'Edit' → swaps body to a CodeMirror block with markdown syntax highlighting, seeded with current `markdown` field
Toggle within edit mode: 'Write' / 'Preview' segmented control; Preview renders the same react-markdown + KaTeX pipeline used in read mode
Footer in edit mode: 'Cancel' (ghost — reverts to original, exits edit mode) | 'Save' (primary — disabled if content unchanged)
Save → PUT /api/courses/[slug]/lessons/[lessonSlug] with the section's markdown patched; on success, exits edit mode and re-renders with new content
On save error (e.g. validation): show inline Callout in danger tone; do not exit edit mode
Editing one section does not lose unsaved edits in another section (per-section local state)
Verify in browser using playwright-skill: click Edit, change text, toggle Preview, save, reload page, confirm new text persists
Typecheck passes

stories.title: Edit widget params — generic forms for quiz / code / demo / sandbox
stories.description: As a course author, I want a per-widget editor for parameters (questions, options, starter code, tests, sigma defaults, etc.) so I can tweak generated content without editing JSON by hand.
acceptanceCriteria: Each non-theory widget gets an 'Edit' icon button (pencil) in its header
Click 'Edit' → opens a side panel (320px from the right edge, slides over content) with a form rendered for the specific widget type
Quiz editor: question textarea, options list (each row: option text + 'correct' checkbox + drag handle + remove button), 'Add option' button, multiSelect toggle, explanation textarea

Code editor: task description (markdown textarea), starter code (CodeMirror Python), tests list — each test row: name input + body (CodeMirror Python collapsible per-row) + remove button, 'Add test' button
Demo editor: image src dropdown (auto-populated from /public/demo-images/), sigmaMin / sigmaMax / sigmaDefault number inputs
Sandbox editor: starter code (CodeMirror) + encouragement text input
Footer: 'Cancel' (ghost) + 'Save' (primary, disabled when content unchanged)
Save → PUT lesson JSON via API; success closes panel and re-renders widget with new data
Validation: client-side Zod parse before sending PUT; field-level error messages rendered inline in red below the offending input
Verify in browser using playwright-skill: edit a quiz's options (rename, mark different one correct, save), retake the quiz with the new options, confirm correct/incorrect logic still works
Typecheck passes

stories.title: Course creation wizard — Stage 1 (Topic) + Stage 2 (Refinement structured form)
stories.description: As a learner starting a new course, I want to enter a topic and answer a few structured questions so the system has enough info to plan the course.
acceptanceCriteria: Route /create is the wizard

Step indicator at top (5 circles connected by 1px line, labels Topic / Refine / Structure / Approve / Generate); active = --accent filled, completed = --success check, future = outlined --border-strong; clicking a completed step jumps back to it

Stage 1 (Topic): centered max-width 640px vertically centered; eyebrow 'What do you want to learn?' (--fs-sm --text-tertiary); big text input (--fs-2xl weight 500, --border underline only — no full border); placeholder cycles through 4 example topics every 3s; below input: 4 chip suggestions ('Backpropagation', 'Linear algebra for ML', 'How GPT works', 'Bayesian statistics') that pre-fill the input on click; 'Next' primary button right-aligned, enabled only when input has ≥3 words; pre-fills from ?topic=… query string when present (for Dashboard empty-state chips)

Stage 2 (Refinement): centered max-width 720px; structured form (no LLM chat in MVP):  'What's your level?' 3 radio button cards (Beginner / Some experience / I know the basics);  'How long should this take?' 3 chip selectors (30 min / An hour / A weekend deep dive);  'Theory or practice?' slider 0–100 with label that updates live ('Mostly theory' / 'Balanced' / 'Mostly practice')
Both stages persist draft to in-memory state (Zustand or React context); refresh resets state
'Back' (ghost left) + 'Next' (primary right) footer; 'Back' from Stage 1 returns to dashboard with confirm dialog if input non-empty
Verify in browser using playwright-skill: fill topic, click Next, fill refine form (level, duration, slider), click Next → lands on Stage 3 placeholder
Typecheck passes

stories.title: Course creation wizard — Stage 3 (Structure cascade)
stories.description: As a learner, I want to see a draft course structure (modules + lessons) and edit it before generation so I can shape what the agent produces.
acceptanceCriteria: Stage 3: 3-column cascade layout — Course | Modules | Lessons
Column 1 (Course): single card showing course title (inline-editable) + 1-line description (inline-editable)

Column 2 (Modules): list of 3-5 module cards seeded with placeholder defaults derived from the topic + level (simple template: 'Module 1: Intro to <topic>', 'Module 2: Core concepts', etc.); each card click selects → highlights + updates Column 3
Drag-to-reorder modules (use @dnd-kit/sortable); '+' button at end of list to add a new module; trash icon on each card to remove (with inline confirm)
Inline rename: click title to edit, blur or Enter to save
Column 3 (Lessons of selected module): list of 4–8 lesson rows (title + 1-line description + estimated minutes); drag-to-reorder, inline rename, +/trash; defaults seeded similarly
All edits persist into the in-memory draft (which becomes course-spec.json on Stage 5)
Sticky bottom bar: 'Back' (ghost) | 'Looks good — generate' (primary) → advances to Stage 4
Verify in browser using playwright-skill: reorder modules via drag-and-drop, rename a lesson, advance to Stage 4, confirm Stage 4 shows updated structure
Typecheck passes

stories.title: Course creation wizard — Stage 4 (Approval) + Stage 5 (Export to course-spec.json)
stories.description: As a learner, I want to review the full course outline and get a clear command to run for generation, so the workflow from spec to generated lessons is unambiguous.
acceptanceCriteria: Stage 4 (Approval): read-only summary of full outline rendered as a clean document — course title + description, then per module: module title, list of lessons with descriptions + estimated minutes, total time estimate; cost-estimate line ('≈ X minutes to generate, Y lessons' computed as lessonCount * 3min as a rough placeholder); big 'Generate course' primary button at bottom

Stage 5 (Export): on click 'Generate course', POST /api/courses with the in-memory draft serialized as CourseSpec; API writes /courses/<slug>/course-spec.json (slug derived via slugify from courseTitle); on 409 (slug collision) prompts user to pick a different title

Stage 5 view: success card with — (a) confirmation 'Course spec saved to /courses/<slug>/course-spec.json'; (b) monospace command block showing the next step: `claude` then invoke `init_course` skill with arg `<slug>` then `./scripts/ralph/ralph.sh`; with 'Copy' button per command; (c) friendly note 'The course will appear on your dashboard once generation completes'; (d) 'Back to dashboard' link

Verify in browser using playwright-skill: walk through wizard end-to-end (Stage 1 → 2 → 3 → 4 → 5), confirm course-spec.json exists at expected path with expected contents (read file post-test and compare to schema)
Typecheck passes

stories.title: Ralph skill: init_course (course-spec → course-prd with research + per-lesson stories)
stories.description: As an agent invoked by the user via Claude Code CLI, I want a SKILL.md that tells me how to convert a course-spec.json into a fresh course-prd.json with research + architect + per-lesson stories so ralph loop can iterate the course generation in separate, focused contexts.
acceptanceCriteria: File: scripts/ralph/skills/init_course/SKILL.md
Frontmatter: name: init_course, user-invocable: true, description triggers on phrases like 'init course', 'generate course from spec', 'create course prd', 'wygeneruj kurs', 'ralph init course'
Skill expects argument: course slug (e.g. 'gauss-basics'); reads /courses/<slug>/course-spec.json, validates it against CourseSpecSchema

Step 1 — Archive existing scripts/ralph/prd.json: if present and branchName differs from `ralph/course-<slug>`, copy current prd.json + progress.txt to scripts/ralph/archive/YYYY-MM-DD-<old-branchName>/ and reset progress.txt with fresh header
Step 2 — Research pass: synthesize key concepts, prerequisites, common misconceptions, suggested ordering for the topic; write to /courses/<slug>/research.md
Step 3 — Architect pass: refine course-spec.draftStructure into final modules + lessons (may merge / split / rename / reorder), write /courses/<slug>/course.json validated against CourseSchema

Step 4 — Generate course-prd.json with stories: US-001 'Compile research notes for course <title>' (output research.md), US-002 'Finalize course structure' (output course.json), US-003..N one per lesson 'Generate lesson: <lesson title>' (output /courses/<slug>/lessons/<lesson-slug>.json) with notes field carrying lesson summary + scope + level context, optional final story 'Review pass: validate all lessons against schema and fix issues'

Each per-lesson story acceptanceCriteria includes: 'Lesson JSON validates against LessonSchema', 'Uses ≥3 widget types where the topic permits', 'Uses generate_lesson skill', 'Typecheck passes' (symbolic — story changes JSON not TS, but kept for ralph's standard validation)
branchName for the new prd.json: `ralph/course-<slug>`
SKILL.md instructs the agent to invoke generate_lesson skill when picking up per-lesson stories
SKILL.md includes a worked example: input course-spec for 'edge-detection-basics', output prd.json structure with research + 4 lessons
SKILL.md follows the same Step/Checklist pattern as scripts/ralph/skills/prd_init/SKILL.md (use it as a template)
Manual smoke test: drop a sample course-spec.json into a test directory, run skill mentally (or live with claude), confirm prd.json structure matches schema
Typecheck passes
stories.notes: Important: while running this skill is acceptable, the user must not be expected to invoke it during MVP development since prd.json IS the MVP plan. Skill is functional for end-users post-MVP-merge.

stories.title: Ralph skill: generate_lesson (lesson plan → validated lesson JSON)
stories.description: As an agent picking up a 'Generate lesson X' story from a course-prd.json, I want a SKILL.md that tells me how to author a single lesson JSON file conforming to widget schemas with a good mix of widget types.
acceptanceCriteria: File: scripts/ralph/skills/generate_lesson/SKILL.md
Frontmatter: name: generate_lesson, user-invocable: false (auto-discovered by ralph agents picking up lesson stories triggered by init_course-generated prd)

Skill instructs agent to: read lesson plan from current ralph story (title + summary + scope from notes/description), read course context from /courses/<slug>/research.md and /courses/<slug>/course.json, read widget JSON Schemas from src/widgets/schemas/

Generation rules documented in SKILL.md: 4–8 sections per lesson; mix widget types (at least 1 theory; 1 quiz where conceptual checking helps; 1 code or 1 demo where topic permits hands-on); theory uses markdown with KaTeX where math is relevant; each code exercise has 2–4 named tests with descriptive names + meaningful (but small) bodies; quiz has plausible distractors and a clear explanation; sandbox encouragement copy is one tasteful sentence

Output written to /courses/<slug>/lessons/<lesson-slug>.json, validated against LessonSchema before commit; on validation failure, agent must read the Zod error, fix the JSON, retry — never commit invalid
SKILL.md includes a worked example: a 4-section lesson on 'Median filter' showing theory + quiz + code (with tests) + sandbox JSON
SKILL.md cross-references init_course skill for context on how the lesson story landed in prd.json
Reviewer can read SKILL.md cold and produce a valid lesson JSON
Typecheck passes

stories.title: Seed course — Podstawy filtrowania Gaussa w wizji komputerowej
stories.description: As a reviewer / first-time user, I want a hand-authored sample course exercising every MVP widget type so the app is demoable end-to-end and serves as a reference for the generate_lesson skill.
acceptanceCriteria: /courses/gauss-basics/course.json validates against CourseSchema; has 1 module with 2 lessons; accentColor: 'indigo'; icon: 'image'

Lesson 1 'Wprowadzenie do filtrowania obrazów' (/courses/gauss-basics/lessons/wprowadzenie-do-filtrowania.json) — 4 sections: theory (intro + co to konwolucja, with one block KaTeX formula and one info Callout), quiz (single-select ABCD: 'Czym jest kernel?' with 4 options + explanation), sandbox (eksperymentuj z numpy: oblicz średnią z 2D array, encouragement set), theory (krótki przegląd typów filtrów — LP/HP, przejście do filtrów Gaussa)

Lesson 2 'Filtr Gaussa w praktyce' (/courses/gauss-basics/lessons/filtr-gaussa-w-praktyce.json) — 5 sections: theory (czym jest Gaussian, math z 2D Gauss formula, callout o właściwościach: separability, izotropowość), demo (Gauss filter na cameraman.jpg, sigma 0.5–8 default 2), code (graded: napisz `gauss_blur(img, sigma)` z 3 testami: 1) sprawdza shape wynikowej tablicy, 2) sprawdza wartości pikseli na fixture, 3) sprawdza obsługę sigma=0 → identity), quiz (multi-select: 'Które stwierdzenia o Gaussie są prawdziwe?' z explanation), sandbox (eksperymentuj ze scipy.ndimage filters)
All lesson JSON files validate against LessonSchema; widget data fields validate against per-widget schemas

Manual integration smoke test (documented in progress.txt): launch dev server, navigate dashboard → seed course → lesson 1, complete each section, advance to lesson 2, complete code exercise (passing all 3 tests), drag demo slider, return to dashboard, confirm progress shows 'In progress · 2/2' or 'Completed' depending on completion
Typecheck passes
stories.notes: Story content is JSON not UI code, but functions as the integration smoke test of all prior widget + view stories. Keep the lesson copy in Polish to match the user's working language.

stories.title: Custom widget extensibility — README + Histogram example widget
stories.description: As a developer adding a new widget type, I want clear documentation and a working example showing the contract, so I can extend the system without touching core code.
acceptanceCriteria: src/widgets/README.md documents the contract: how to add a new widget type — (1) add a CSS var --widget-<name> in tokens.css, (2) define Zod data schema in src/widgets/<Name>/schema.ts and export JSON Schema via build:schemas, (3) add an entry to widgetRegistry with { component, label, icon (lucide name), accentVar }, (4) add a per-widget editor form (per US-023 pattern), (5) optionally extend SectionSchema discriminated union

Example custom widget: src/widgets/Histogram/HistogramWidget.tsx takes { binEdges: number[], counts: number[] }, renders SVG histogram + a single horizontal slider that selects one bin and shows its count + range as a callout; visual style follows Demo widget conventions
Histogram widget registered in widgetRegistry under type='histogram' with a fresh --widget-histogram CSS var (a tasteful muted color distinct from existing widget accents)
Histogram widget editor form added per the US-023 pattern (binEdges editable as comma-separated number list, counts likewise)

One section using histogram added to seed course Lesson 2 (between demo and code, e.g. 'Histogram intensywności pikseli przed/po rozmyciu' with two histogram widgets) — validates against LessonSchema (histogram added to discriminated union)
Verify in browser using playwright-skill: navigate to seed course Lesson 2, scroll to histogram section, confirm widget renders with its accent rail and the slider selects bins correctly
Typecheck passes
